answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing jobs whose results are independently checked and whose payment is released after a dispute window. A mirror agent that copies a real worker’s claims cannot simply mint trust: each accepted job needs a distinct scarce resource, such as a bonded deposit, and repeated failures forfeit it. Sybils must therefore lock up capital and perform useful work, or risk losing the bond; spinning up identities alone buys no reputation. A wharf or garden may host many agents, but neither grants them extra weight.
